h1: The 8 Best All-in-One Printers for Home Use of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best all-in-one printers for home use, from budget Canon and HP inkjets to an ink-tank Brother and a feeder-equipped model.
mainKeyword: all in one printer for home use
summary: The Canon PIXMA TR8620a is the do-everything home printer, with fax, a feeder, AirPrint and Alexa. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the better value for feeder and duplex, the Canon TS4320 is the cheap duplex pick, and the Brother MFC-J4355DW suits envelopes and ink-tank economics.
intro: An all-in-one printer is only as good as the features you will actually use. Buyers pay for fax and a feeder, then discover their home needs a duplex unit and a quiet one.
We ranked eight all-in-ones on the listing details: functions, feeder, duplex, display and ink approach. Start with what you do weekly, then pick the cheapest model that covers it.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Nearly every all-in-one feature, in one home-friendly body.
products.description:
The TR8620a prints, copies, scans and faxes, with an automatic feeder, AirPrint and Android support, Alexa compatibility, and both photo and document printing. Wireless is built in and it falls in the $100-200 range.

We put it first because no other pick here lists as many features. Households that will use them get more value than from the cheaper units.

Take it if you scan, fax and print photos. Skip it if your needs are simple, since you would pay for unused hardware.
products.idealFor: Households that use most all-in-one features.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: ADF and duplex for home-office work without the fax extras.
products.description:
With a feeder, duplex printing, AI-capable features and a three-month Instant Ink trial, the 8125e is aimed at home-office users. Wireless is standard and the price bucket is $50-100.

It lands behind the Canon only because it skips fax and the extra mobile options. For feeder-plus-duplex needs it is the best value here.

Choose it for steady document work. Keep in mind the ink trial lasts only three months.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The same feeder-and-duplex idea, listed at a higher price bucket.
products.description:
This 8125 variant lists the same feeder, duplex printing, AI-capable features and Instant Ink trial as the 8125e, and falls in the $100-200 bucket.

It is third because the listing shows a higher price for the same headline features. If the two are priced equally on the day, either is fine.

Buy whichever 8125 costs less. Do not assume the higher-priced one adds anything.
products.idealFor: Buyers who find this variant at a good price.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex printing in a compact single-tray body.
products.description:
The TS4320 prints, scans and copies with duplex printing and a single compact tray, backed by a one-year limited warranty. Setup is described as easy, and it is in the $50-100 group.

It places fourth because it has no feeder, which the HP units above include. In return it is smaller and cheaper.

Pick it for light home use with two-sided printing. It will not handle stacks of pages to scan.
products.idealFor: Light home use with two-sided printing.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen makes daily use less fiddly.
products.description:
Along with print, scan, copy and duplex printing, the TS6520 adds a tiny OLED screen and an intuitive control panel. No feeder is included, and the price bucket is $50-100.

It sits fifth because the extra screen is a comfort feature and the TS4320 offers the same core functions for less thought.

Good for anyone who dislikes app-only control. It cannot feed pages automatically.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder and fax for households that scan multi-page papers.
products.description:
Printing, scanning, copying and faxing are all here, with an automatic feeder and mobile printing support, in a compact home design. It costs in the $50-100 range.

It ranks sixth because duplex is not listed, which the HP units offer along with a feeder. It does undercut them on size.

Pick it if you scan multi-page forms. You will flip pages manually for two-sided jobs.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Print, scan and copy with simple setup, nothing more.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 offers 3-in-1 functions, simple wireless setup, a compact budget design and a three-month Instant Ink trial. There is no feeder, and it costs $50-100.

It is seventh because it has fewer features than the Canon models. It does the basics well.

Good for occasional home use. Not for heavy document work.
products.skipIf: You need a feeder or duplex.

products.name: Brother INKvestment 4355 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer (MFC-J4355DW)
products.verdict: Ink-tank economics and a manual feed slot for specialty paper.
products.description:
The MFC-J4355DW prints, scans and copies, uses an ink-tank system, has a 1.8 inch color display and a manual feed slot for envelopes and cardstock, with a Refresh Subscription trial. It is the priciest at $200-500.

It ranks last because it costs far more than the rest and has no feeder listed. Its niche is specialty paper.

Buy it if you print envelopes and cardstock often. Caveat: the high price.

methodology.description: Compact, easy-setup models scored above office-heavy ones.

methodology.title: Ink approach
methodology.description: Instant Ink trials, ink-tank systems and subscriptions were noted.

methodology.description: Displays and control panels were weighed for daily ease.

methodology.title: Price bracket
methodology.description: Each printer was judged against its bucket.

whatMatters.detail: A feeder pulls pages through the scanner without lifting the lid each time. It matters for multi-page forms. Look for ADF in the title or specs.
Duplex prints both sides automatically. It saves paper. Check the listing for duplex.
Instant Ink and similar programs are trials here, lasting three months for the HP models. Plan ongoing ink costs beyond the trial.
A small screen lets you operate without an app. This matters for quick copies. Check for display size.
A manual feed slot takes envelopes and cardstock. It matters only if you print them often. Look for manual feed in the specs.

howToChoose.intro: Pick by the job you do most.

cards.label: Cartridge inkjets
cards.text: Lower cost upfront. The Canon and HP models.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: Built for lower running costs. The Brother MFC-J4355DW.

howToChoose.note: Most households should default to a cartridge inkjet unless they print weekly.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Simple setup, mobile printing and photo ability.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon TR8620a handles photos, AirPrint and Alexa.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use fax, a feeder and photos. The Canon TR8620a pulls them together.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The HP DeskJet 4355 covers basics.

faq.a: Only if you scan multi-page documents. For single pages it adds cost.
Paying for fax and a feeder that never gets used.
The three-month trials only cover the start. Check ongoing cost.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use the maker's app to join your wifi and install the driver.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles healthy?
faq.a: Print something periodically so ink does not dry out.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone?
faq.a: The Canon TR8620a lists AirPrint and Android, and the TR4720 lists mobile printing.

finalTake: The Canon PIXMA TR8620a is the full-featured home printer. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the sensible mid-range pick for feeder and duplex. Choose the Canon TS4320 for light use and the Brother only for envelopes.
